method: Every pinned Greek verse read before authoring. All verses drafted before reading prior Fluent. TSW is a post-authoring comparator, not a wording template. Each authored verse has its own rationale. F0–F3 choices are provisional; no independent review or change quota.

verses.rationale: Retain the death metaphor and the perfect participle's accomplished coming without identifying the event.
verses.before: Jesus said to them, “Truly I tell you, some standing here will not taste death before they see the kingdom of God having come with power.”
verses.after: He went on to say, “Truly I tell you, some standing here will not taste death before they see that the kingdom of God has come in power.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And he was saying to them, “Truly I say to you, there are some standing here who will not taste death until they see the kingdom of God having come in power.”

verses.rationale: Keep the exact interval and three named witnesses; divide the ascent and transformation for oral clarity.
verses.before: Six days later Jesus took Peter, James, and John with him and led them up a high mountain by themselves. He was transfigured before them,
verses.after: Six days later Jesus took Peter, James, and John up a high mountain, where they were alone. There, before their eyes, he was transformed.
verses.tsw_comparator: And after six days Jesus took with him Peter and James and John, and brought them up on a high mountain by themselves. And he was transfigured before them,

verses.rationale: Retain the earthly craft comparison and exceptional whiteness without adding the absent snow comparison.
verses.before: and his clothes became dazzling white, whiter than anyone on earth could bleach them.
verses.after: His clothes shone an intense white, whiter than any launderer on earth could make them.
verses.tsw_comparator: and his garments became radiant, exceedingly white, such as no fuller on earth is able to whiten.

verses.rationale: Preserve Mark's order of Elijah and Moses and make the plural speakers clear.
verses.before: Elijah appeared to them with Moses, and they were talking with Jesus.
verses.after: Elijah appeared to them with Moses, and the two were talking with Jesus.
verses.tsw_comparator: And Elijah appeared to them with Moses, and they were speaking with Jesus.

verses.rationale: Keep Rabbi, the proposed three shelters, and each recipient rather than interpret the shelters as a festival observance.
verses.before: Peter said to Jesus, “Rabbi, it is good for us to be here. Let us make three shelters—one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.”
verses.after: Peter said to Jesus, “Rabbi, it is good for us to be here. Let us put up three shelters: one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And answering, Peter said to Jesus, “Rabbi, it is good for us to be here. Let us make three tents, one for you and one for Moses and one for Elijah.”

verses.rationale: Retain the explanation of Peter's speech and the change from his uncertainty to their shared fear.
verses.before: He did not know what to say because they were terrified.
verses.after: He did not know what to say, for they were terrified.
verses.tsw_comparator: For he did not know what to say, for they were terrified.

verses.rationale: Make the two linked events audible and retain beloved Son and the command to listen.
verses.before: Then a cloud came and overshadowed them, and a voice came from the cloud: “This is my beloved Son. Listen to him.”
verses.after: A cloud came over them, and a voice spoke from the cloud: “This is my beloved Son. Listen to him!”
verses.tsw_comparator: And a cloud came, overshadowing them, and a voice came out of the cloud, “This is my beloved Son; listen to him.”

verses.rationale: Carry the abrupt disappearance and Jesus alone without adding an explanation.
verses.before: Suddenly, when they looked around, they no longer saw anyone with them except Jesus alone.
verses.after: Suddenly they looked around and saw no one with them but Jesus.
verses.tsw_comparator: And suddenly, looking around, they saw no one with them any longer except Jesus alone.

verses.rationale: Name the subject after the scene shift and retain the resurrection condition on silence.
verses.before: As they were coming down the mountain, Jesus ordered them not to tell anyone what they had seen until the Son of Man had risen from the dead.
verses.after: As they came down the mountain, Jesus ordered them to tell no one what they had seen until the Son of Man had risen from the dead.
verses.tsw_comparator: And as they were coming down from the mountain, he ordered them to tell no one what they had seen, except when the Son of Man should rise from the dead.

verses.rationale: Keep both their restraint and their unresolved discussion; repeat the resurrection wording.
verses.before: They kept the matter to themselves, discussing what “rising from the dead” might mean.
verses.after: They kept the matter to themselves, discussing what “rising from the dead” meant.
verses.tsw_comparator: And they held the matter to themselves, questioning what the rising from the dead might be.

verses.rationale: Render the interrogative idiom as why while preserving scribes and must.
verses.before: They asked him, “Why do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?”
verses.after: They asked him, “Why do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?”
verses.tsw_comparator: And they were asking him, saying, “Why do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?”

verses.rationale: Retain the difficult relationship between Elijah's restoration and the Son of Man's suffering as a question.
verses.before: He said to them, “Elijah does come first and restores all things. Yet how is it written about the Son of Man that he must suffer many things and be treated with contempt?
verses.after: He replied, “Elijah does come first to restore everything. Yet how is it written about the Son of Man that he must suffer greatly and be treated with contempt?
verses.tsw_comparator: And he said to them, “Elijah indeed comes first and restores all things. And how is it written of the Son of Man that he should suffer many things and be treated with contempt?

verses.rationale: Preserve the unidentified they and scriptural claim without inserting John by name.
verses.before: But I tell you that Elijah has come, and they did to him whatever they wanted, just as it is written about him.”
verses.after: But I tell you, Elijah has already come, and they did whatever they wanted to him, just as it is written about him.”
verses.tsw_comparator: But I say to you that Elijah has come, and they did to him whatever they wished, just as it is written of him.”

verses.rationale: Follow the plural arrival and seeing in the pinned source; other clarifies the disciples left below.
verses.before: When they came to the other disciples, they saw a large crowd around them and scribes arguing with them.
verses.after: When they reached the other disciples, they saw a large crowd around them and scribes arguing with them.
verses.tsw_comparator: And coming to the disciples, they saw a great crowd around them and scribes arguing with them.

verses.rationale: Resolve the object pronoun and retain immediate astonishment without inventing a reason for it.
verses.before: As soon as the whole crowd saw Jesus, they were greatly amazed. They ran to him and greeted him.
verses.after: As soon as the crowd saw Jesus, everyone was astonished and ran to greet him.
verses.tsw_comparator: And immediately all the crowd, seeing him, were greatly amazed, and running up, greeted him.

verses.rationale: Retain the two parties in the question while leaving their exact identification open.
verses.before: He asked them, “What are you arguing with them about?”
verses.after: He asked them, “What are you arguing with them about?”
verses.tsw_comparator: And he asked them, “What are you arguing with them about?”

verses.rationale: Divide the introduction and condition; render the speechless spirit by its effect here without a medical diagnosis.
verses.before: Someone from the crowd answered, “Teacher, I brought you my son, who has a spirit that makes him unable to speak.
verses.after: Someone in the crowd answered, “Teacher, I brought you my son. He has a spirit that keeps him from speaking.
verses.tsw_comparator: And one from the crowd answered him, “Teacher, I brought my son to you, having a mute spirit;

verses.rationale: Preserve the sequence of violent symptoms, the spirit as agent, and the disciples' inability.
verses.before: Whenever it seizes him, it throws him down. He foams, grinds his teeth, and becomes rigid. I asked your disciples to cast it out, but they could not.”
verses.after: Whenever it seizes him, it throws him down. He foams at the mouth, grinds his teeth, and becomes rigid. I asked your disciples to drive it out, but they could not.”
verses.tsw_comparator: and wherever it seizes him, it throws him down, and he foams and grinds his teeth and becomes rigid. And I asked your disciples to cast it out, but they were not able.”

verses.rationale: Keep the repeated how long and plural rebuke rather than direct blame only at the father.
verses.before: Jesus answered, “O faithless generation, how long will I be with you? How long will I put up with you? Bring him to me.”
verses.after: Jesus answered them, “You faithless generation! How long must I stay with you? How long must I put up with you? Bring him to me.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And answering them he said, “O faithless generation, how long shall I be with you? How long shall I bear with you? Bring him to me.”

verses.rationale: Resolve the repeated pronouns and keep the spirit as the one reacting to Jesus.
verses.before: They brought the boy to him. When the spirit saw Jesus, it immediately convulsed the boy. He fell on the ground and rolled around, foaming.
verses.after: They brought the boy to him. When the spirit saw Jesus, it immediately threw the boy into convulsions. He fell to the ground and rolled about, foaming at the mouth.
verses.tsw_comparator: And they brought him to him. And seeing him, immediately the spirit convulsed the boy, and falling on the ground, he rolled, foaming.

verses.rationale: Name Jesus for the question and preserve the father's chronological answer.
verses.before: Jesus asked his father, “How long has this been happening to him?” The father said, “From childhood.
verses.after: Jesus asked his father, “How long has this been happening to him?” “Since childhood,” he answered.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he asked his father, “How long has this been happening to him?” And he said, “From childhood.

verses.rationale: Retain destructive intent and the father's plural us, setting up Jesus' response to if you can.
verses.before: It has often thrown him into fire and water to destroy him. But if you can do anything, have compassion on us and help us.”
verses.after: “Often it has thrown him into fire and water to destroy him. But if you can do anything, have compassion on us and help us!”
verses.tsw_comparator: And often it has cast him both into fire and into water, to destroy him. But if you are able to do anything, have compassion on us and help us.”

verses.rationale: Mark Jesus' echo of the father's words as a quotation; keep the unqualified possibility saying.
verses.before: Jesus said to him, “‘If you can’? Everything is possible for the one who trusts.”
verses.after: Jesus said to him, “‘If you can’? Everything is possible for the one who believes.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And Jesus said to him, “‘If you are able’—all things are possible for the one who believes.”

verses.rationale: Preserve the coexistence of faith and unbelief and omit tears and Lord absent from this source.
verses.before: Immediately the child’s father cried out, “I trust; help my unbelief!”
verses.after: At once the boy's father cried out, “I believe! Help my unbelief!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Immediately the father of the child cried out and said, “I believe; help my unbelief!”

verses.rationale: Make the described effects intelligible and retain the explicit command and permanent prohibition.
verses.before: When Jesus saw a crowd running together, he rebuked the unclean spirit: “You mute and deaf spirit, I command you, come out of him and never enter him again.”
verses.after: When Jesus saw a crowd rushing toward them, he rebuked the unclean spirit: “Spirit that keeps him from speaking and hearing, I command you: come out of him and never enter him again!”
verses.tsw_comparator: And Jesus, seeing that a crowd was running together, rebuked the unclean spirit, saying to it, “You mute and deaf spirit, I command you, come out of him and enter him no more.”

verses.rationale: Distinguish the spirit's departure from the boy's resulting condition and retain most rather than all.
verses.before: After crying out and convulsing him violently, the spirit came out. The boy became like a corpse, so that many said, “He is dead.”
verses.after: The spirit cried out, convulsed the boy violently, and came out. The boy lay like a corpse, so that most of the people said, “He is dead.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And crying out and convulsing him terribly, it came out, and he became like a corpse, so that most said, “He has died.”

verses.rationale: Keep the physical action and paired raising/standing verbs without declaring an actual death.
verses.before: But Jesus took him by the hand, raised him up, and he stood.
verses.after: But Jesus took him by the hand and raised him up, and he stood.
verses.tsw_comparator: But Jesus, taking him by the hand, raised him, and he stood up.

verses.rationale: Retain the private setting and disciples' question about their own inability.
verses.before: When Jesus entered the house, his disciples asked him privately, “Why could we not cast it out?”
verses.after: After Jesus had gone indoors, his disciples asked him privately, “Why could we not drive it out?”
verses.tsw_comparator: And when he had entered the house, his disciples were asking him privately, “Why were we not able to cast it out?”

verses.rationale: Follow the shorter pinned reading with prayer alone; do not import fasting.
verses.before: He told them, “This kind cannot come out by anything except prayer.”
verses.after: He told them, “This kind can come out only through prayer.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And he said to them, “This kind is not able to come out by anything except prayer.”

verses.rationale: Keep the travel and wish for secrecy, allowing the reason to continue into the next verse.
verses.before: They left there and passed through Galilee. Jesus did not want anyone to know,
verses.after: They left that place and traveled through Galilee. Jesus did not want anyone to know,
verses.tsw_comparator: And going out from there, they were passing through Galilee, and he did not want anyone to know,

verses.rationale: Preserve the handing-over passive, the human-hands image, repeated killing, and Mark's three-days-later sequence.
verses.before: because he was teaching his disciples: “The Son of Man is being handed over into human hands. They will kill him, and after he is killed, three days later he will rise.”
verses.after: for he was teaching his disciples. He told them, “The Son of Man is being handed over to human hands. They will kill him, and after he is killed, he will rise three days later.”
verses.tsw_comparator: for he was teaching his disciples, saying to them, “The Son of Man is being handed over into the hands of men, and they will kill him, and when he has been killed, after three days he will rise.”

verses.rationale: Keep ignorance and fear as distinct responses without supplying their motives.
verses.before: But they did not understand the saying and were afraid to ask him.
verses.after: They did not understand what he meant and were afraid to ask him.
verses.tsw_comparator: But they did not understand the saying, and they were afraid to ask him.

verses.rationale: Keep the arrival, house, and road connection while identifying the questioner.
verses.before: They came to Capernaum. When Jesus was in the house, he asked them, “What were you discussing on the way?”
verses.after: They came to Capernaum. Once inside the house, Jesus asked them, “What were you discussing on the road?”
verses.tsw_comparator: And they came to Capernaum. And when he was in the house, he asked them, “What were you discussing on the way?”

verses.rationale: Make the explanatory because audible and retain the silence following the status dispute.
verses.before: But they were silent because on the way they had argued with one another about who was greatest.
verses.after: They said nothing, because on the road they had been arguing about which of them was greatest.
verses.tsw_comparator: But they were silent, for on the way they had argued with one another about who was the greatest.

verses.rationale: Keep the teaching posture and the repeated of all in the reversal of status.
verses.before: Jesus sat down, called the twelve, and said, “If anyone wants to be first, that person must be last of all and servant of all.”
verses.after: Jesus sat down, called the Twelve, and said, “Anyone who wants to be first must be last of all and servant of all.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And sitting down, he called the twelve and said to them, “If anyone wants to be first, he shall be last of all and servant of all.”

verses.rationale: Retain both placing and embracing without assigning the child a gender absent from the Greek noun.
verses.before: He took a child, placed the child among them, and then took the child in his arms.
verses.after: He took a child and stood the child among them. Then, holding the child in his arms, he said,
verses.tsw_comparator: And taking a child, he set him in the midst of them, and taking him in his arms, he said to them,

verses.rationale: Preserve the repeated welcome and the widening relation to the sender; not only expresses the contextual contrast.
verses.before: He said, “Whoever welcomes one such child in my name welcomes me. And whoever welcomes me welcomes not only me but the one who sent me.”
verses.after: “Whoever welcomes one child like this in my name welcomes me. And whoever welcomes me welcomes not only me but the one who sent me.”
verses.tsw_comparator: “Whoever receives one such child in my name receives me, and whoever receives me receives not me but the one who sent me.”

verses.rationale: Retain us as the stated boundary and the attempted/preventive force of the imperfect verb.
verses.before: John said to him, “Teacher, we saw someone casting out demons in your name, and we tried to stop him because he was not following us.”
verses.after: John said to him, “Teacher, we saw someone driving out demons in your name. We tried to stop him because he was not following us.”
verses.tsw_comparator: John said to him, “Teacher, we saw someone casting out demons in your name, and we tried to stop him, because he was not following us.”

verses.rationale: Carry the command and quick reversal idiom without equating the outsider with a formal disciple.
verses.before: Jesus said, “Do not stop him. No one who does a work of power in my name can soon afterward speak evil of me.
verses.after: “Do not stop him,” Jesus said. “No one who does a deed of power in my name can turn around and speak evil of me.
verses.tsw_comparator: But Jesus said, “Do not stop him, for no one who does a mighty work in my name will be able soon after to speak evil of me.

verses.rationale: Retain the source's repeated us and compact proverbial wording.
verses.before: Whoever is not against us is for us.
verses.after: For whoever is not against us is for us.
verses.tsw_comparator: For the one who is not against us is for us.

verses.rationale: Express the stated ground of the gift and emphatic assurance without adding in my name from another reading.
verses.before: Truly I tell you, whoever gives you a cup of water to drink because you belong to Christ will certainly not lose their reward.
verses.after: Truly I tell you, anyone who gives you a cup of water because you belong to the Messiah will certainly not lose their reward.”
verses.tsw_comparator: For whoever gives you a cup of water to drink because you belong to Christ, truly I say to you, he will not lose his reward.”

verses.rationale: Retain little ones, belief, stumbling, and the disturbing comparison; specify millstone size in a note.
verses.before: But whoever causes one of these little ones who trust in me to stumble, it would be better for that person if a large millstone were hung around their neck and they were thrown into the sea.
verses.after: “If anyone causes one of these little ones who believe in me to stumble, it would be better for that person to have a great millstone hung around their neck and be thrown into the sea.
verses.tsw_comparator: “And whoever causes one of these little ones who believe to stumble, it would be better for him if a great millstone were hung around his neck and he were thrown into the sea.

verses.rationale: Preserve the severe bodily image and the repeated destination rather than turn the command into explanation.
verses.before: If your hand causes you to stumble, cut it off. It is better for you to enter life maimed than to have two hands and go into Gehenna, into the unquenchable fire.
verses.after: If your hand causes you to stumble, cut it off. It is better to enter life with one hand than to have both hands and go into Gehenna, into the fire that cannot be put out.
verses.tsw_comparator: And if your hand causes you to stumble, cut it off; it is better for you to enter into life maimed than having two hands to go into Gehenna, into the unquenchable fire.

verses.rationale: Keep the parallel image while following this verse's shorter source wording without a fire clause.
verses.before: If your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off. It is better for you to enter life lame than to have two feet and be thrown into Gehenna.
verses.after: If your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off. It is better to enter life lame than to have both feet and be thrown into Gehenna.
verses.tsw_comparator: And if your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off; it is better for you to enter into life lame than having two feet to be thrown into Gehenna.

verses.rationale: Preserve the shift from life to kingdom of God and continue the sentence into the quotation.
verses.before: If your eye causes you to stumble, tear it out. It is better for you to enter the kingdom of God with one eye than to have two eyes and be thrown into Gehenna,
verses.after: If your eye causes you to stumble, throw it away. It is better to enter the kingdom of God with one eye than to have two eyes and be thrown into Gehenna,
verses.tsw_comparator: And if your eye causes you to stumble, cast it out; it is better for you to enter into the kingdom of God with one eye than having two eyes to be thrown into Gehenna,

verses.rationale: Retain the plural possessive and the Isaiah image without changing worm into an abstraction.
verses.before: where their worm does not die and the fire is not quenched.
verses.after: where their worm does not die and the fire is not put out.
verses.tsw_comparator: where their worm does not die and the fire is not quenched.

verses.rationale: Leave the difficult salt/fire metaphor open and omit the longer sacrificial addition absent from the source.
verses.before: For everyone will be salted with fire.
verses.after: For everyone will be salted with fire.
verses.tsw_comparator: For everyone will be salted with fire.

verses.rationale: Keep the connected salt images and plural community command without supplying a single interpretation.
verses.before: Salt is good, but if salt loses its saltiness, how will you season it? Have salt in yourselves and be at peace with one another.”
verses.after: Salt is good, but if salt loses its saltiness, how will you season it? Have salt in yourselves, and live at peace with one another.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Salt is good; but if the salt becomes unsalty, with what will you season it? Have salt in yourselves, and be at peace with one another.”

verses.rationale: Retain both geographical phrases and repeated again; do not reconstruct an unstated route.
verses.before: Jesus left there and went to the region of Judea and beyond the Jordan. Crowds gathered around him again, and as was his custom, he taught them.
verses.after: Jesus left there and went to the region of Judea and beyond the Jordan. Crowds gathered around him again, and again he taught them, as he usually did.
verses.tsw_comparator: And rising from there, he went into the region of Judea and beyond the Jordan, and crowds gathered to him again; and again, as was his custom, he was teaching them.

verses.rationale: Follow the pinned text's unnamed plural questioners rather than import Pharisees from a variant.
verses.before: Some Pharisees came to test him and asked, “Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife?”
verses.after: They asked him, “Is a man allowed to divorce his wife?” They were putting him to the test.
verses.tsw_comparator: And Pharisees came and, testing him, asked, “Is it lawful for a man to divorce his wife?”

verses.rationale: Keep command distinct from the permission in their answer.
verses.before: He answered them, “What did Moses command you?”
verses.after: He answered, “What did Moses command you?”
verses.tsw_comparator: And answering, he said to them, “What did Moses command you?”

verses.rationale: Preserve written certification and dismissal as two linked actions with explicit referents.
verses.before: They said, “Moses permitted a man to write a certificate of divorce and send her away.”
verses.after: They said, “Moses allowed a man to write a certificate of divorce and send his wife away.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And they said, “Moses permitted a man to write a certificate of divorce and to send her away.”

verses.rationale: Keep hardness of heart as the reason for the command without softening the rebuke.
verses.before: Jesus said, “Because of your hardness of heart he wrote this command for you.
verses.after: Jesus told them, “He wrote you this command because your hearts were hard.
verses.tsw_comparator: But Jesus said to them, “Because of your hardness of heart he wrote this commandment for you.

verses.rationale: Retain the creation contrast and quotation; do not insert God as an explicit noun absent here.
verses.before: But from the beginning of creation, ‘Male and female he made them.’
verses.after: But from the beginning of creation, ‘he made them male and female.’
verses.tsw_comparator: But from the beginning of creation, ‘male and female he made them.’

verses.rationale: Carry the source's joining clause despite its variant markers and continue the quotation across verse numbers.
verses.before: ‘For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife,
verses.after: ‘For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife,
verses.tsw_comparator: ‘For this reason a man shall leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife,

verses.rationale: Retain one flesh as the repeated embodied image rather than replace it with a relationship abstraction.
verses.before: and the two will become one flesh.’ So they are no longer two but one flesh.
verses.after: and the two will become one flesh.’ So they are no longer two, but one flesh.
verses.tsw_comparator: and the two shall become one flesh.’ So they are no longer two but one flesh.

verses.rationale: Make the inference clear and render generic human agency inclusively.
verses.before: Therefore, what God has joined together, let no human being separate.”
verses.after: Therefore, what God has joined together, no human being should separate.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Therefore what God has joined together, let no human being separate.”

verses.rationale: Preserve the renewed question and private narrative setting without adding content to their question.
verses.before: In the house, the disciples asked him about this again.
verses.after: Back in the house, the disciples asked him about this again.
verses.tsw_comparator: And in the house the disciples asked him again about this.

verses.rationale: Retain the male subject, remarriage, and against her rather than erase the wife's place in the saying.
verses.before: He said to them, “Whoever divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery against her,
verses.after: He told them, “Anyone who divorces his wife and marries another woman commits adultery against her.
verses.tsw_comparator: And he said to them, “Whoever divorces his wife and marries another commits adultery against her;

verses.rationale: Preserve the corresponding female agency and do not import an exception from another Gospel.
verses.before: and if she divorces her husband and marries another, she commits adultery.”
verses.after: And if a woman divorces her husband and marries another man, she commits adultery.”
verses.tsw_comparator: and if she divorces her husband and marries another, she commits adultery.”

verses.rationale: Clarify the purpose and Jesus as recipient while retaining the disciples' rebuke.
verses.before: People were bringing children to Jesus so that he might touch them, but the disciples rebuked them.
verses.after: People were bringing children to Jesus for him to touch, but the disciples rebuked them.
verses.tsw_comparator: And they were bringing children to him, so that he might touch them; but the disciples rebuked them.

verses.rationale: Retain indignation and both positive and negative commands; leave such as these broader than the children alone.
verses.before: When Jesus saw this, he was indignant and said, “Let the children come to me. Do not stop them, because the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.
verses.after: When Jesus saw this, he was indignant. “Let the children come to me,” he said. “Do not stop them, for the kingdom of God belongs to such as these.
verses.tsw_comparator: But when Jesus saw it, he was indignant and said to them, “Let the children come to me; do not hinder them, for to such belongs the kingdom of God.

verses.rationale: Retain the child comparison and strong negative without defining childlike qualities.
verses.before: Truly I tell you, whoever does not receive the kingdom of God like a child will certainly not enter it.”
verses.after: Truly I tell you, whoever does not receive the kingdom of God like a child will never enter it.”
